plan: Given my private value of $24, I should bid slightly above half of my value to maximize expected profit, while considering the risk of overpaying. A rational strategy is to bid slightly less than $24, as bidding exactly my value or higher would yield no profit. I aim to outbid a potential third-highest bid without exceeding my value. Since this is the only round, I focus solely on this auction's outcome.

Given my private value of $9, I should bid slightly less than my value to maximize potential profit while minimizing loss. Since bids are in $0.1 increments, a rational approach is to bid slightly lower than my value, such as $8.9, to ensure a potential win while not exceeding my value. This strategy accounts for rational opponents who will not bid above their values.

Given my value of $13, I should bid slightly below my value to maximize potential profit while minimizing risk. Since the prize value is independently drawn, other bidders are likely to have different values. A rational bid slightly below $13, say $12.9, increases my chance of winning if others bid low, while not exceeding my value. This ensures I pay less than my value if I win, maximizing profit.
